items.title: Show HN: Simple self-hosted LLM assistant with user-steered compounding context
items.why_it_matters: A developer open-sourced a lightweight LLM assistant built on Cloudflare Workers that manages conversation context by saving simple, user-steered topic summaries instead of using complex RAG. This is highly relevant because you are building AI-ingest to manage your own information flow, and keeping context clean is a major hurdle. This week, you can clone the repository, run it locally, and inspect their summary-saving logic to see if you can adapt a similar lightweight context strategy for your own Next.js and Supabase app.

items.title: Show HN: Neal – Codex writes the code, Claude reviews it
items.why_it_matters: A developer released Neal, a CLI orchestrator designed to let Codex write code while Claude acts as an adversarial reviewer to catch hallucinations and bugs. This directly targets your exact workflow of directing Claude and Codex, helping you manage larger features without the AI losing track of the codebase. This week, you can install the CLI and run it on a small, isolated feature branch of your AI-ingest project to see if the dual-agent setup improves your code quality.

items.title: What should go in your Claude.md?
items.why_it_matters: A new guide outlines how to structure a `claude.md` file to give Claude Code and other agents persistent, project-specific instructions. Since you are vibe-coding, having a clear set of rules prevents Claude from hallucinating packages or suggesting backend structures that don't match your Next.js and Supabase stack. This week, you can create a `claude.md` file in the root of your AI-ingest repo containing your stack preferences so Claude Code aligns with your setup on every prompt.

items.title: Show HN: Implement-spec – a harness-agnostic spec-to-verified-PR agent skill
items.why_it_matters: Implement-spec is a new open-source agent skill that takes a written markdown specification and automatically generates a verified, tested Pull Request. Since you are actively learning Git and GitHub commit discipline on AI-ingest, this tool helps automate the transition from idea to clean code branch. This week, write a simple markdown spec for a minor UI tweak in your project, run this tool against it, and let it generate a clean PR for you to review and merge.

items.title: Agent skills that bring team coding standards to Claude Code and Codex
items.why_it_matters: This repository introduces reusable agent skills designed to enforce team coding and git standards directly inside Claude Code and Codex. As you focus on getting better at directing AI and maintaining clean repository discipline, these skills automate the tedious parts of verification. This week, you can import these skills into your local Claude Code configuration to automatically lint your code and format your commit messages before they go to GitHub.

items.title: Claude Code can read plaintext secrets even when Read is denied
items.why_it_matters: A security analysis revealed that Claude Code can sometimes read plaintext secrets (like API keys) in your workspace even when explicit read permissions are restricted. Because you are using Supabase and likely have local environment variables, a leak could compromise your database. This week, open your AI-ingest project and double-check that your `.env.local` file is explicitly added to both your `.gitignore` and `.claudeignore` files.
